method: OPEN AND QUOTED, from the RCH Melbourne Clinical Practice Guideline 'Jaundice in early infancy' (Updated June 2026), retrieved 2026-09-23. Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. LICENCE: Free to read but NOT openly licensed -- each page carries '(c) 2026 The Royal Children's Hospital'. Quoted with attribution on the same footing as the 14 RCH guidelines and the Immunisation Handbook guidelines already in this compendium.

claims.claim: **Measure, don't eyeball:** if significant jaundice is suspected, do a transcutaneous bilirubinometer (TcB) and/or serum bilirubin. Visual assessment alone is unreliable.
claims.source_text: If significant jaundice is clinically suspected, a transcutaneous bilirubinometer (TcB) and/or serum bilirubin level should be performed. Visual assessment alone is unreliable for estimating bilirubin level
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Jaundice in early infancy' (Updated June 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Jaundice_in_early_infancy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Most jaundice is physiological and benign**, but ⚠️ severe unconjugated hyperbilirubinaemia can cause acute bilirubin encephalopathy and kernicterus, with permanent neurological injury.
claims.source_text: Most jaundice is physiological and benign, however severe unconjugated hyperbilirubinaemia may lead to acute bilirubin encephalopathy and kernicterus, which can cause permanent neurological injury
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Jaundice in early infancy' (Updated June 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Jaundice_in_early_infancy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Pathological features:** onset under 24 hours · rapidly rising bilirubin · unwell appearance · prolonged jaundice · conjugated hyperbilirubinaemia · evidence of haemolysis.
claims.source_text: Features suggestive of pathological jaundice include onset <24 hours of age, rapidly rising bilirubin, unwell appearance, prolonged jaundice, conjugated hyperbilirubinaemia, or evidence of haemolysis
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Jaundice in early infancy' (Updated June 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Jaundice_in_early_infancy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Pale or acholic stools at any age need urgent evaluation** for cholestatic liver disease, including biliary atresia.
claims.source_text: Pale or acholic stools at any age require urgent evaluation for cholestatic liver disease, including biliary atresia
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Jaundice in early infancy' (Updated June 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Jaundice_in_early_infancy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Risk factors for severe hyperbilirubinaemia:** prematurity · poor feeding · dehydration · excessive weight loss · haemolysis · bruising/cephalhaematoma.
claims.source_text: Risk factors for severe hyperbilirubinaemia include prematurity, poor feeding, dehydration, excessive weight loss, haemolysis, bruising/cephalhaematoma
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Jaundice in early infancy' (Updated June 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Jaundice_in_early_infancy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **In the history:** onset under 24 hours; **over 2 weeks is prolonged**; poor weight gain or weight loss over 10% in the first week of life.
claims.source_text: Age of onset <24 hours Duration >2 weeks is prolonged … Poor weight gain/significant weight loss >10% in first week of life
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Jaundice in early infancy' (Updated June 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Jaundice_in_early_infancy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Jaundice may be less obvious in infants with darker skin.**
claims.source_text: Pattern and degree of jaundice (may be less obvious in infants with darker skin)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Jaundice in early infancy' (Updated June 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Jaundice_in_early_infancy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **TcB can screen well infants ≥35 weeks' gestation and ≥24 hours old.** Confirm with SBR if within 50 micromol/L of the treatment threshold, ≥250 micromol/L, rapidly rising, or phototherapy is being considered or has started. TcB is less reliable after phototherapy.
claims.source_text: TcB may be used as a screening tool in well infants ≥35 weeks gestation ≥24 hours old should be confirmed with SBR if: within 50 micromol/L of treatment threshold ≥250 micromol/L Rapidly rising Phototherapy is being considered or has commenced reliability decreases following phototherapy
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Jaundice in early infancy' (Updated June 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Jaundice_in_early_infancy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **SBR is the gold standard** for diagnosis and treatment decisions; interpret it by gestation, postnatal age and risk factors on a gestation-specific nomogram.
claims.source_text: SBR Gold standard for diagnosis and treatment decisions … Levels should be interpreted according to gestation, postnatal age and clinical risk factors using an appropriate gestation-specific nomogram
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Jaundice in early infancy' (Updated June 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Jaundice_in_early_infancy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Request fractionated bilirubin** in prolonged jaundice, unwell infants, suspected pathological jaundice, pale stools or dark urine.
claims.source_text: Fractionated bilirubin (unconjugated/conjugated) should be performed in prolonged jaundice, unwell infants, suspected pathological jaundice, pale stools or dark urine
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Jaundice in early infancy' (Updated June 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Jaundice_in_early_infancy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Most well infants with unconjugated jaundice need no further investigation.** Physiological jaundice starts after 24 hours, peaks on day 3–5 and lasts 1–2 weeks.
claims.source_text: The majority of well infants with unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia do not require further investigation or management … Physiological jaundice Majority of well infants Onset after 24 hours Peaks day 3-5, lasts 1-2 weeks
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Jaundice in early infancy' (Updated June 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Jaundice_in_early_infancy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Early onset (under 24 hours) is pathological:** every infant needs fractionated SBR, FBE and a direct antiglobulin test (DAT).
claims.source_text: Early onset: (<24 hours) Pathological All should have: SBR (fractionated) FBE Direct antiglobulin test (DAT)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Jaundice in early infancy' (Updated June 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Jaundice_in_early_infancy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Prolonged jaundice (over 2 weeks):** fractionated SBR, FBE with film and reticulocytes, TFTs, blood group, DAT; LFTs if conjugated bilirubin is over 10%.
claims.source_text: Prolonged (>2 weeks) All should have: SBR (fractionated) FBE, film and reticulocytes TFTs Blood Group DAT LFTs if conjugated bilirubin >10%
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Jaundice in early infancy' (Updated June 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Jaundice_in_early_infancy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Conjugated hyperbilirubinaemia (any age) — over 20 µmol/L or over 20% of total: refer to gastroenterology.** A normal ultrasound does not exclude biliary atresia.
claims.source_text: Conjugated hyperbilirubinaemia (at any age) Conjugated bilirubin >20 µmol/L or >20% of total bilirubin Refer to gastroenterology … Note: a normal ultrasound does not exclude biliary atresia
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Jaundice in early infancy' (Updated June 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Jaundice_in_early_infancy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Breast milk jaundice** occurs in healthy, thriving breast-fed infants: onset 5–7 days, peaks at 2–3 weeks, can last up to 12 weeks — a **diagnosis of exclusion**.
claims.source_text: Breast milk jaundice In healthy, thriving breast-fed infants Typical onset 5-7 days after birth Peaks at 2-3 weeks, can last up to 12 weeks Diagnosis of exclusion after considering above causes
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Jaundice in early infancy' (Updated June 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Jaundice_in_early_infancy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Plot TcB/SBR on a gestation-specific nomogram and use local treatment thresholds.** Judge severity by gestation, postnatal age, bilirubin, clinical condition, hydration and risk factors.
claims.source_text: Severity of jaundice should be assessed according to gestation, postnatal age, bilirubin level, clinical condition, hydration status and risk factors … TcB/SBR should be plotted on an appropriate gestation-specific nomogram. Refer to local bilirubin treatment thresholds
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Jaundice in early infancy' (Updated June 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Jaundice_in_early_infancy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Support hydration and feeding**, especially in breast-fed infants and those with excessive weight loss or poor intake; consider a lactation consultant and maternal and child health nurse.
claims.source_text: Ensure adequate hydration and feeding support, particularly in breast-fed infants and those with excessive weight loss or poor intake. Consider lactation consultant and maternal and child health nurse involvement
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Jaundice in early infancy' (Updated June 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Jaundice_in_early_infancy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Phototherapy follows local protocol** (intensity, biliblanket, monitoring), with close monitoring of weight, hydration and bilirubin and serial SBR until resolution.
claims.source_text: Refer to local protocol regarding phototherapy intensity, biliblanket use and monitoring … Ongoing close monitoring of weight, hydration, and bilirubin levels should be performed during treatment as per local protocol, with serial checks of SBR to ensure resolution of hyperbilirubinaemia
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Jaundice in early infancy' (Updated June 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Jaundice_in_early_infancy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Exchange transfusion only in, or with, a Neonatal Intensive Care Unit** — contact the paediatric retrieval service.
claims.source_text: Exchange transfusion Should only be performed in, or in conjunction with, a Neonatal Intensive Care Unit Contact local paediatric retrieval service for support
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Jaundice in early infancy' (Updated June 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Jaundice_in_early_infancy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Breast milk jaundice: do NOT stop breastfeeding.** It may last up to 12 weeks; no further bilirubin levels are needed unless the jaundice is worsening.
claims.source_text: Breast milk jaundice Diagnosis of exclusion Do NOT stop breastfeeding May last up to 12 weeks, no further bilirubin levels necessary unless jaundice is deemed to be worsening
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Jaundice in early infancy' (Updated June 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Jaundice_in_early_infancy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Sepsis: treat immediately with IV antibiotics** as per the sepsis guideline.
claims.source_text: Sepsis Immediate treatment as per SEPSIS – assessment and management with IV antibiotics
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Jaundice in early infancy' (Updated June 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Jaundice_in_early_infancy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Extrahepatic obstruction or neonatal hepatitis is uncommon, but early diagnosis improves outcome** — discuss with paediatric gastroenterology if suspected.
claims.source_text: Extrahepatic obstruction or neonatal hepatitis Uncommon but early diagnosis improves outcome If suspected discuss with local paediatric gastroenterology services
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Jaundice in early infancy' (Updated June 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Jaundice_in_early_infancy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Involve the paediatric team** if the child is unwell, the cause is unclear, or conjugated bilirubin is over 20% of total.
claims.source_text: Consider consultation with local paediatric team when Child is unwell Cause of jaundice is unclear Conjugated bilirubin is >20% of total level
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Jaundice in early infancy' (Updated June 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Jaundice_in_early_infancy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consider transfer** if the level is rising despite adequate local treatment, or the child needs exchange transfusion.
claims.source_text: Consider transfer when Jaundice level rising despite adequate treatment offered at local centre Child needs exchange transfusion
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Jaundice in early infancy' (Updated June 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Jaundice_in_early_infancy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge when** SBR/TcB is below the treatment threshold with follow-up planned, causes needing treatment are excluded, and the infant is well and feeding well.
claims.source_text: Consider discharge when SBR/TcB below the treatment threshold and plan in place for follow-up Causes requiring further treatment or investigation have been excluded Clinically well and feeding well
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Jaundice in early infancy' (Updated June 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Jaundice_in_early_infancy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Sunlight exposure is not a treatment for jaundice.**
claims.source_text: Sunlight exposure is not recommended as a treatment for jaundice
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Jaundice in early infancy' (Updated June 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Jaundice_in_early_infancy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Arrange early MCH nurse and/or GP follow-up**, especially if under 7 days old, exclusively breastfeeding or still establishing feeds, or the level is borderline. **Re-check bilirubin in 24–48 hours** if borderline or still rising.
claims.source_text: Arrange early follow-up with maternal and child health nurse and/or GP to ensure adequate oral intake, especially if <7 days old exclusively breastfeeding or still establishing adequate oral feeds bilirubin level is borderline for requiring treatment … Re-check bilirubin in 24-48 hours if borderline level or still rising
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Jaundice in early infancy' (Updated June 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Jaundice_in_early_infancy/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Tell parents to seek review** if jaundice persists 2–3 weeks without an established cause, they think it is worsening, or they have any other concern.
claims.source_text: Parents should be advised to seek medical review if jaundice is present for 2-3 weeks and cause has not previously been established parents believe jaundice is worsening or there is any other cause for clinical concern
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Jaundice in early infancy' (Updated June 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Jaundice_in_early_infancy/, retrieved 2026-09-23
